adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:166 — `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes raw input, not uniqueGuests, so already-existing attendees get a full AttendeeScheduledEmail re-invite [conf=100,P1]

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that are already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted). However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the raw input `guests`, not `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the `newGuests` array to decide per attendee: if `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` it sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (full re-invite), otherwise it sends `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (notification). Therefore, if the input includes an email that was already an attendee (alongside at least one truly new guest so the request passes), that existing attendee will incorrectly be treated as a “new guest” and receive a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` re-invite. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:44 — no booking.status check; guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings, triggering calendar updates and CONFIRMED ics emails for a dead event [conf=100,P1]

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler fetches the booking by id and proceeds to update attendees (prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany), calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking), and sends emails whose ICS payload explicitly sets status: "CONFIRMED" (see attendee/organizer add-guests email templates). There is no conditional check on any booking status/state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) before performing these side effects, so callers can add guests to bookings regardless of whether the booking is effectively inactive, causing calendar updates and "CONFIRMED" ICS notifications to be sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:44 — no past-booking check; adding a guest to a finished booking re-invites every attendee to a past event [conf=75,P2]

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation fetches the booking (including `startTime`/`endTime`) and then always (1) updates DB attendees, (2) calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and (3) calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. There is no guard that prevents these side effects when the booking has already ended (e.g., `booking.endTime < now`). As written, a user can add guests to an already-finished booking and the handler will still send emails/ICS updates to attendees and update connected calendars for a past event. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:145 — seated events: no BookingSeat row created and seatsPerTimeSlot capacity never enforced, yielding seatless attendees and overbooking [conf=75,P1]

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation simply appends new records to `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and does not reference any seat-related persistence (e.g., a `BookingSeat` model/table) or seat-capacity enforcement logic. While the handler does pass through `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` into the CalendarEvent object, the diff provides no verifiable contract that adding “guests” must create seat rows or be constrained by `seatsPerTimeSlot` (guests may be distinct from “seats” in this codebase). Therefore the claim about missing `BookingSeat` rows and overbooking is not directly verifiable from the diff and relies on assumptions about external seat semantics.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx onError, `message` is built with a template literal: `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. Template literals always produce a string, even when `err.data?.code` is undefined (e.g., "undefined: ...") or when `t(err.message)` is empty. Since non-empty strings are truthy, `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` will virtually never hit the fallback, so users may see raw/undesired codes like "BAD_REQUEST: ..." or "undefined: ..." instead of the friendly fallback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:74-92 — check-then-insert TOCTOU: attendee read and insert are in separate un-transacted queries with no FOR UPDATE and no idempotency key; concurrent calls both insert [conf=100,P1]

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `addGuestsHandler` first reads the booking (including current `attendees`) via `findFirst`, then computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already present in that *previously-read* attendee list, and only afterwards performs the write via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`. There is no transaction wrapping the read+write, no row locking (`FOR UPDATE`), and no `createMany({ skipDuplicates: true })` or other idempotency mechanism. Under concurrent requests adding the same guest(s), both can pass the initial “not already an attendee” check and both attempt to insert, leading to duplicate attendee rows (if the DB allows it) or a runtime error due to a uniqueness constraint (if one exists). This is a real TOCTOU correctness issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:76 — case-sensitive `guest === attendee.email` against a lowercased blacklist; Foo@x.com bypasses both dedupe and blacklist [conf=100,P1]

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the blacklist is normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but each incoming `guest` is compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. This makes the blacklist check case-sensitive, so `Foo@x.com` would not match a blacklisted `foo@x.com`. Similarly, the dedupe check `guest === attendee.email` is also case-sensitive and can allow duplicates differing only by case. Both issues are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:20-42 — no status/endTime guard and no WHERE guard on the update at :92; terminal (cancelled) state is re-reachable and pushes calendar invites [conf=75,P1]

addGuests.handler.ts:158-165 — EventManager is built from the acting user's credentials while the event belongs to booking.userId, so attendee/team-admin callers silently no-op or fail the calendar sync [conf=75,P1]

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to run (team admin/owner and even attendees via `isAttendee`). However the calendar sync is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, i.e., using the acting caller’s credentials, not the booking owner’s (`booking.userId`) credentials. The handler even loads `booking.user.credentials` in the initial query but never uses them. For calls made by an attendee or a team admin who is not the booking owner, this is a concrete mismatch: the calendar event being updated belongs to the booking/organizer context, but the sync is attempted with the caller’s credentials, which can reasonably fail or do nothing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:92-165 — DB commit precedes an un-transacted external calendar mutation with no timeout/retry/compensation; a throw leaves DB and calendar divergent and skips emails entirely [conf=75,P1]

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({... attendees.createMany ...})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`, which is an external side-effect. That call is not wrapped in a try/catch and there is no transaction/compensation logic tying the DB write to the calendar update. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (network/API error), the handler will abort after the DB has been updated, leaving the DB and external calendar potentially inconsistent and preventing the later `sendAddGuestsEmails` from running at all (it’s after that await). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no .max(); one call materializes unbounded inserts, attendee list, and email fan-out [conf=100,P2]

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is an unbounded `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()`. The new `addGuestsHandler` then (1) does `attendees.createMany` with all provided emails, (2) builds `attendeesList` via `Promise.all` over all attendees, and (3) calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which fans out emails across `calendarEvent.attendees` plus organizer/team members. Since neither the client (`AddGuestsDialog` / `MultiEmail`) nor the server schema caps the array length, a single request can trigger arbitrarily large DB inserts and email sending work. This is a verifiable resource-abuse/performance/spam risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:539-546 — `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is O(n·m) list membership inside a map over all attendees; should be a Set [conf=100,P2]

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the code maps over `calendarEvent.attendees` and for each attendee executes `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. Since `includes` on an array is linear in `newGuests.length`, this makes the overall work O(attendeesCount * newGuestsCount). This is directly verifiable from the diff and can be improved by converting `newGuests` to a `Set` for O(1) membership checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:168 — `guests` vs `uniqueGuests` have diverged in meaning under one name, so filtered-out addresses are still classified "new" by email-manager.ts:540 [conf=100,P2]

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out already-attending and blacklisted emails, and only `uniqueGuests` are actually persisted via `createMany`. However the email step calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (original unfiltered input). In email-manager.ts:sendAddGuestsEmails, it classifies attendees as “new” by checking `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. Because `guests` may include addresses that were *not* added (already existed / blacklisted), those attendees will still match the `includes` check and be misclassified as new, causing the wrong email template to be sent. Passing `uniqueGuests` instead would align the meaning with the actual newly-added attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:527-546 — unbounded Promise.all with no concurrency limit or per-email isolation; one rejection poisons the batch and the caller swallows it with console.log [conf=75,P2]

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `sendAddGuestsEmails` in `packages/emails/email-manager.ts`, which builds an array of sendEmail promises (organizer + each team member + each attendee) and executes them with `await Promise.all(emailsToSend);`. This has (1) no concurrency limiting, so a booking with many attendees/team members can trigger an unbounded parallel send burst, and (2) Promise.all will reject the whole batch if any single send fails. Additionally, the new caller in `addGuests.handler.ts` wraps `sendAddGuestsEmails` in a try/catch that only `console.log`s a generic message and does not propagate or handle partial failures, matching the finding’s “caller swallows it” concern. These behaviors are directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` contradicts the isTeamAdminOrOwner name, and `teamId ?? 0` uses 0 as a magic sentinel in a real FK lookup [conf=75,P2]

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code sets `isTeamAdminOrOwner` using `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This is a verifiable mismatch with the variable name and typical intended semantics: it will only be true if the user is BOTH a team admin and the team owner, which is much stricter than “admin OR owner” and can incorrectly deny access. Also, `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` passes a hardcoded `0` into `isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner`, which is a magic sentinel for a real FK lookup and could cause incorrect permission behavior if `teamId` is null/undefined.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:145 — seatsPerTimeSlot is copied into the event but never enforced as a write precondition, so seated events can be overfilled [conf=75,P2]

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler`, guests are appended to `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` with no check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or any other capacity constraint) before writing. Yet the handler does copy `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` into the constructed `CalendarEvent` (`evt`), which implies the booking may be a seated event. As written, this endpoint can add an arbitrary number of attendees to an existing booking, potentially exceeding the seat limit for that time slot/booking type. This is a concrete correctness/business-logic gap visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:26 — `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` bare-indexes a possibly-empty array and throws inside the subject template [conf=75,P2]

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts` the subject template interpolates `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. If `this.calEvent.attendees` is empty, `this.calEvent.attendees[0]` is `undefined` and accessing `.name` will throw at runtime while generating the email payload. Nothing in this new template or the surrounding email-manager code defensively guarantees a non-empty attendees array (the `CalendarEvent` type allows an empty array, and this file itself has no guard), so this is a real correctness risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:24 — uniqueness is enforced only client-side, so an e2e test through the dialog goes green while any direct tRPC caller inserts duplicates [conf=75,P2]

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: server-side `addGuestsHandler` does not enforce uniqueness of `guests` within the request. The input schema (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts`) only validates email format, and `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)` only filters out emails already present on the booking or blacklisted—duplicates within `guests` will pass through unchanged. Thus a direct tRPC caller can submit `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` and both entries can be sent to `attendees.createMany`. The dialog adds a client-only zod `refine` uniqueness check, so UI/e2e via dialog may pass while API allows duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:108-118 — `await getTranslation(...)` inside a .map over every attendee: one call per attendee instead of per distinct locale [conf=75,P3]

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `attendeesListPromises` is built via `bookingAttendees.attendees.map(async (attendee) => ({ ... language: { translate: await getTranslation(attendee.locale ?? "en", "common"), ... } }))`. This performs an `await getTranslation(...)` per attendee, even when multiple attendees share the same locale (e.g., all defaulting to "en"). That is a verifiable inefficiency introduced by the diff and can add unnecessary repeated I/O/work for larger attendee lists; it could be optimized by caching translations per distinct locale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:60 — `id: booking.userId || 0` with findFirstOrThrow turns a null userId into an opaque Prisma throw for user 0 [conf=75,P3]

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the organizer is fetched with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. The same handler treats `booking.user` as optional elsewhere (`booking?.user?.destinationCalendar`), implying `booking.userId` can be null/undefined. If `booking.userId` is null, this code silently substitutes `0` and then `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma "not found" error for user id 0, rather than a clear, intentional error about a missing organizer/invalid booking. This is a verifiable correctness/robustness issue introduced by the fallback-to-0 pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:169 — email failure is swallowed and the mutation still returns success, so the UI reports "Guests added" when nobody was notified [conf=100,P3]

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:52 — transitive privilege escalation: every added guest becomes an attendee and can then add more third parties to a private booking, with no organizer consent or revocation path [conf=75,P1]

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization explicitly allows any current attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the guard only forbids when `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`. Since added guests are persisted into `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, any newly added guest can subsequently call this mutation and add further third parties. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 — new guests get AttendeeScheduledEmail embedding the booking uid cancel/reschedule links and videoCallData.password, leaking capability tokens to parties the organizer never authorized [conf=75,P1]

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:168 — blacklisted addresses filtered from the DB write are still passed to sendAddGuestsEmails and still receive booking mail with cancel/reschedule links [conf=75,P2]

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, blacklisted emails are removed into `uniqueGuests` and only `uniqueGuests` are written to the DB (createMany). The email recipients for `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` come from `evt.attendees`, which is built from `bookingAttendees.attendees` (the post-update DB attendees). Since blacklisted addresses were never created as attendees, they are not in `evt.attendees` and therefore will not be emailed at all. Passing the original `guests` array only affects the `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` check for attendees that actually exist in `evt.attendees` (e.g., could misclassify existing attendees), but it does not cause blacklisted addresses to receive mail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:4 — no .max() on guests and no rate limiting; one request sends thousands of ICS-attached emails from the instance's trusted domain (spam amplification, reputation burn) [conf=75,P2]

adjudication.rationale: The new endpoint `viewer.bookings.addGuests` accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound (`.max(...)`) in `addGuests.schema.ts`, and the handler unconditionally `createMany` attendees and then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` builds `emailsToSend` including organizer/team emails plus one email per `calendarEvent.attendees` entry, so a large `guests` array can trigger a large number of outbound emails (with ICS payloads) from the instance’s domain. No throttling/rate limiting or per-request cap is shown in the diff for this mutation, making spam/abuse amplification a verifiable risk introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:158-165 — the calendar write uses the calling user's third-party credentials against the organizer's booking references, driving an attendee's integrations with another user's external event ids [conf=50,P2]

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, calendar updates are performed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user`/`credentials` come from `ctx.user` (the *caller*), not the booking’s organizer (`booking.userId` / `booking.user.credentials`). Since the mutation explicitly allows an attendee to call it (`isAttendee` check), an attendee can trigger `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using their own third‑party credentials while operating on a booking that belongs to another user. This is a real correctness/authorization risk introduced by the diff: the calendar write is not bound to the organizer’s integrations and may update the wrong external calendar or fail to update the organizer’s event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:88 — createMany creates Attendee rows with no BookingSeat reference on seats-enabled bookings, yielding orphaned attendees invisible to every seat-keyed path and silent overbooking [conf=75,P1]

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:73 — case-sensitive dedupe against a lowercased blacklist inserts duplicate Attendee rows for an existing participant [conf=75,P2]

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the `uniqueGuests` filter compares emails with strict equality: `guest === attendee.email` and checks `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. However `blacklistedGuestEmails` is explicitly lowercased while `guest` is not, so a blacklisted email can bypass the check by changing case. Similarly, the “already an attendee” check is case-sensitive and can allow inserting a second attendee row for the same logical email if the existing attendee email casing differs (unless the DB guarantees normalized casing/unique constraints, which is not shown in the diff). This is a real correctness defect introduced by inconsistent email normalization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:88 — dedup read and createMany are not transactional and Attendee has no unique constraint on (bookingId,email); concurrent submits both insert [conf=50,P2]

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the code reads the current attendees (`prisma.booking.findFirst(... include: { attendees: true })`), computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against that in-memory list, then performs a separate `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`. There is no transaction wrapping the read+write and no `skipDuplicates`/upsert logic, so two concurrent submissions can both pass the dedupe check and then both attempt to insert the same attendee emails, resulting in duplicate attendee rows (if no DB unique constraint) or a runtime insert error (if a unique constraint exists). The race/non-atomicity is directly verifiable from the diff; the specific claim about the schema lacking a unique constraint is not shown here but the concurrency hazard remains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` accepts [], so an empty array reaches the handler and surfaces as BAD_REQUEST "emails_must_be_unique_valid" instead of a validation error [conf=100,P3]

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/src/templates/AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.tsx:3, OrganizerAddGuestsEmail.tsx:3 — `{...props}` spread after title/subject/headerType lets caller values silently override the intended add-guests strings [conf=75,P3]
